meta.name: Manage catering event quotes and countdowns with Postgres, Gmail, OpenAI and Telegram

name: automate catering event orders with AI quotes and countdown reminders

parameters.content:
## 09-09-01 automate catering event orders with AI quotes and countdown reminders

### How it works

Keep catering events on track from inquiry to invoice.

- A new event arrives on the intake webhook. Validation rejects bad payloads, an AI assistant writes a quote email to the client, and the event is stored with its deposit deadline.
- When the client replies with changes or pays the deposit, the update webhook updates the record and confirms by email while the owner gets a Telegram alert.
- On event day the completion webhook saves the final headcount and the AI writes the final invoice email plus a review request.
- Every morning at 08:00 a countdown sweep finds events at T-7, T-3, T-1 and overdue deposits, emails clients, pings the owner, and posts an all clear on quiet days.

### Setup steps

- Create the catering_events and comms_log tables in Postgres and connect the credential.
- Add Gmail, Telegram and OpenAI credentials, then point the three webhooks at your intake channel.
- Replace ops@yourcatering.com and YOUR_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID with real values.

### Customization

- Edit packages and payment terms in Build Quote Context; change sweep thresholds in Parse Open Events. Rules are deterministic; the AI only writes the copy.

## Intake and quote

A new event lands on the intake webhook, validation rejects bad payloads, the AI writes the quote email, and the event is stored with its deposit deadline.

## Updates and deposit

Clients reply with changes (headcount, menu, venue, date) or pay the deposit. The workflow updates the record, confirms by email and alerts the owner on Telegram.

## Completion and invoicing

When the event is done, the final headcount is saved, the AI writes the invoice and review request, and both are emailed to the client.

## Daily countdown sweep

Every morning the sweep finds events at T-7, T-3, T-1 and overdue deposits, emails clients, pings the owner, and posts an all clear when nothing is due.

={{ 'A catering inquiry was rejected because required fields were missing (client name, email, event type or a valid event date).

Name: ' + (($json.body && $json.body.client_name) || $json.client_name || '-') + '
Email: ' + (($json.body && $json.body.client_email) || $json.client_email || '-') + '
Event: ' + (($json.body && $json.body.event_type) || $json.event_type || '-') + '
Date: ' + (($json.body && $json.body.event_date) || $json.event_date || '-') }}

options.systemMessage: You are the quoting assistant for a small catering company. Write a warm, professional quote email to a prospective client. Reference the package options that fit their menu notes and budget, state that a 30 percent deposit confirms the date and is due by the deposit deadline, and note that final prices depend on the confirmed headcount. Plain text email, 140 to 220 words, friendly and concrete, no hype, no sales pressure. Use plain punctuation only (no em dashes, no en dashes). Return ONLY valid JSON with keys: subject (a short subject line under 12 words) and body (the full email text).

parameters.query: INSERT INTO catering_events (event_id, client_name, client_email, event_type, event_date, guest_count, venue, menu_notes, budget_range, status, deposit_status, deposit_due_date, quote_sent_at, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6,$7,$8,$9,'quoted','pending',$10,$11,NOW(),NOW()) RETURNING event_id, client_name, client_email, $12::text AS qsubj, $13::text AS qbody;
INSERT INTO comms_log (event_id, comm_type, recipient, subject, body, direction, sent_at) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,'to_client',$6) RETURNING event_id;

parameters.text: ={{ 'New catering inquiry ' + $json.event_id + ': ' + $json.event_type + ', ' + $json.guest_count + ' guests on ' + $json.event_date + ' (' + $json.client_name + '). Quote sent. Deposit due ' + $json.deposit_due_date }}

parameters.text: ={{ 'The event is complete. Write the final invoice email and a short review request email for this catering client.\n\n' + $json.event_summary }}

options.systemMessage: You are the invoicing assistant for a small catering company. Write a warm, professional final invoice email and a short review request email. The invoice email thanks the client, notes the event date, compares the quoted guest count with the final headcount, states that the deposit was already received and the balance is settled per the agreed terms, and invites questions. The review request email is 2 to 3 sentences asking how the food and service were, and simply asks them to hit reply. Plain text, no hype, no em dashes, no en dashes. Return ONLY valid JSON with keys: invoice_subject (under 12 words), invoice_body, review_subject (under 12 words), review_body.

parameters.query: UPDATE catering_events SET status = 'invoiced', final_headcount = $1::int, updated_at = NOW() WHERE event_id = $2::text RETURNING event_id, client_name, client_email, $3::text AS isubj, $4::text AS ibody, $5::text AS rsubj, $6::text AS rbody;
INSERT INTO comms_log (event_id, comm_type, recipient, subject, body, direction, sent_at) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,'to_client',$6) RETURNING event_id;
INSERT INTO comms_log (event_id, comm_type, recipient, subject, body, direction, sent_at) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,'to_client',$6) RETURNING event_id;

parameters.text: ={{ 'Event completed ' + $json.event_id + ' (' + $json.client_name + '). Final headcount ' + $json.final_headcount + '. Invoice and review request sent to client.' }}

parameters.query: SELECT COALESCE((SELECT json_agg(row_to_json(c))::text FROM catering_events c WHERE c.status NOT IN ('invoiced', 'cancelled') AND c.deposit_status IS NOT NULL), '[]') AS evs;
INSERT INTO comms_log (event_id, comm_type, recipient, subject, body, direction, sent_at) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6,$7) RETURNING event_id;
UPDATE catering_events SET last_nudge_at = $1::text, updated_at = NOW() WHERE event_id = $2::text;
